reasoning: A 120 mm square-based vase with ~1 mm walls (section 1.98 mm), no overhangs, no bridges. Purely cosmetic — the outside surface is the product. Two things will make or break it: (1) the outer wall finish, because that's what's seen, and (2) the layer resolution, because a vase is a curved surface and staircase artefacts read as defects. Everything else — supports, brim, infill — is irrelevant here: zero overhang area means no support; a 2825 mm² footprint at 2× slenderness is well-adhered; and walls this thin leave no room for infill lines regardless of the density setting.

changes.reason: the outside is the visible surface and a vase is a curved form; 0.12 mm layers halve the step height that would otherwise show as ridges on the exterior
the exterior wall is the finished surface; dropping from the 160 ceiling to 100 gives the extruder time to lay down a consistent, glossy line instead of a rippled one

design_notes: If the vase has a lip or lip-geometry on the rim that overhangs past 45°, a small chamfer or bevel on that feature in the CAD would let it print without support and give a cleaner edge than a support scar.
